title: Composition on the Image
statement: Let $M,U$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $f,g$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $T_1,T_2:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $M$ computes $f$ on every input $x$ within $T_1(|x|)$ steps, and for every $x$, $U$ computes $g(x)$ from input $f(x)$ within $T_2(|x|)$ steps. Then there is a finite Boolean Turing machine $N$ that computes $g$ on every input within $2T_1(n)+T_2(n)+2$ steps for inputs of length $n$.
hypotheses_covered: Functions $f,g$ from Boolean words to Boolean words
$U$ computes $g(x)$ from $f(x)$ within $T_2(|x|)$ steps for every $x$
replaced:
Let $M$ and $U$ be multi-tape Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let
$f$ and $g$ be functions on Boolean words, and let
$T_1, T_2 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be arbitrary.  Suppose $M$ computes $f$
in time $T_1$, meaning that on every input $x$ it halts within $T_1(\abs{x})$
steps with output $f(x)$, and suppose that for every Boolean word $x$ the
machine $U$ on input $f(x)$ halts within $T_2(\abs{x})$ steps with output
$g(x)$, the budget being measured at the length of the original word $x$.
Then there is a machine $N$ over the Boolean alphabet that computes $g$ in
time $n \mapsto 2\,T_1(n) + T_2(n) + 2$; no monotonicity of $T_2$ is required,
and $U$ need not halt on words outside the image of $f$.
